name: Thanksgiving
hook: Pilgrims, Lincoln, parades and pie — the holiday's facts repeat on Jeopardy.

facts.label: William Bradford
facts.statement: William Bradford, governor of Plymouth Colony, proclaimed a 1621 day of Thanksgiving and invited Native Americans to a three-day feast.

facts.label: Abraham Lincoln
facts.statement: Abraham Lincoln issued the proclamation that made the last Thursday in November a national day of Thanksgiving.

facts.label: Macy's parade
facts.statement: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade debuted in New York City in 1924, conceived by store employees.

facts.label: Cyber Monday
facts.statement: Cyber Monday, the Monday after Thanksgiving, is named for its online shopping bargains.

facts.label: turkey
facts.statement: Turkey is the traditional Thanksgiving bird; the Beltsville Small White is a breed, and turducken stuffs a chicken into a duck into a turkey.

facts.label: stuffing
facts.statement: Stuffing is the bread-based Thanksgiving side most likely to be made with sage.

facts.label: Canada
facts.statement: Canada has celebrated Thanksgiving on the second Monday in October since 1957.
